newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank sees more crown liberalisation in 97.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank sees more crown liberalisation in 97.

text.p: Slovakia will take major steps to achieve full capital account convertibility of its currency, the crown, by the end of next year, Peter Balaz, head of debt management at the National Bank of Slovakiam said on Monday.

He said important steps for further liberalising the capital account included meeting criteria for joining the OECD and freeing entrepreneurs from a requirement to exchange all foreign currency earnings into local currency.
"These will be the most important steps towards further liberalisation of capital account convertibility," Balaz told a capital markets conference.
The central bank freed the crown for all current account transactions late last year.
A further move towards full convertibility will be the gradual relaxation of rules covering foreign borrowing and persuading companies to seek foreign capital with non-sovereign guarantees, he said.

"The present need to obtain NBS permission for foreign credits is a big disadvantage for borrowers and we understand the need to liberalise this," Balaz said, adding the permission requirement affected only companies and not banks.

"The relaxation will affect long and medium-term loans at first, but short-term loans, which we consider dangerous, from the point of view of maintaining our monetary targets, will remain subject to NBS approval," he added.
Balaz said companies needed to alter their philosophy on foreign borrowing and rely on their own guarantees for their credits rather than seek state guarantees.

He added that NBS activities in the past three years had contributed to stabilising Slovakia's foreign exchange rate regime and the level of its foreign exchange reserves resulting in achieving favourable credit ratings from the main rating agencies.
